subtopics.title: Charter, Mandate and Leadership
subtopics.summary: The US is constituting a Board of Peace, a US-led inter-governmental body established under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025) and linked to the 20-point Gaza peace plan. Its charter has 13 Articles, and its chair is the US President. The Board's mandate covers supervising Gaza's civil and security bodies, mobilising assistance and ensuring accountability during Gaza's transition.
facts: Type: US-led inter-governmental body
Established under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025)
Charter contains 13 Articles on membership, financial contributions and dispute redressal
Mandate: supervise and guide NCAG (civil administration) and ISF (security)
Mandate: mobilise international financial and technical assistance
Mandate: ensure transparency, coordination and accountability during transition
Chair: US President Donald Trump, who also serves separately as Inaugural Representative of the US
Chair can be removed only if he resigns voluntarily or is unanimously declared incapable by the Executive Board
Executive Board includes former UK PM Tony Blair, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, World Bank President Ajay Banga and Jared Kushner
US announced the Board meets with 19 countries; India is absent from this high-level initiative

subtopics.title: Membership and Gaza Governance Bodies
subtopics.summary: Membership of the Board requires a country to consent to be bound by its charter, and it is offered on a rotational or a permanent basis. Gaza's civil administration is handled by the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), with Nickolay Mladenov as High Representative linking the Board and the NCAG on the ground. The Gaza Executive Board is a supporting operational body that coordinates on-the-ground activities.
facts: Membership requires a country to consent to be bound by the Charter
Rotational membership: 3-year tenure without mandatory financial contribution
Permanent membership: available through a reported contribution of USD 1 billion
Initial authorisation of the Board lasts until 31 December 2027
High Representative for Gaza: Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, on-the-ground liaison between Board and NCAG
NCAG: 15-member committee of politically independent Palestinian technocrats
NCAG is chaired by Ali Shaath, a former Palestinian Authority Deputy Minister
NCAG is responsible for day-to-day civil administration
Gaza Executive Board: supporting operational body that coordinates on-the-ground activities
Gaza Executive Board members: US, UK, Turkey, Qatar, Egypt, UAE, Cyprus and Netherlands; no Palestinian representative

subtopics.title: Key Features of the US 20-point Gaza Plan
subtopics.summary: The US plan, officially titled the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, envisions a demilitarised Gaza with an immediate ceasefire and the release of all hostages. It pairs security arrangements, including the International Stabilization Force (ISF), with humanitarian aid and reconstruction through a special economic zone. The plan excludes Hamas from governance while offering amnesty to members who decommission their weapons.
facts: Gaza is envisioned as a demilitarised, terror-free zone
An immediate ceasefire is mandated, halting military actions by both sides
All hostages, alive or deceased, must be released within 72 hours of Israel's formal acceptance
Israel frees 250 Palestinian life-sentence prisoners and 1,700 detainees
Hamas members who decommission weapons get amnesty or safe passage abroad
Full humanitarian aid enters immediately; Rafah crossing reopens under agreement
Special economic zone with favourable trade terms, supported by international investment
No forced displacement: people are free to stay, leave or return
Hamas is excluded from governance; ISF deployed to secure Gaza and train police
Interfaith dialogue platform created to promote religious harmony

subtopics.title: UN Reform and the Board's Significance
subtopics.summary: Reform of the UN system is treated as urgent because ad hoc peacebuilding missions end once crises subside and UN Security Council reform is deadlocked. The booklet presents the Board as an incremental innovation within existing structures, using the General Assembly's power under Article 22 of the UN Charter. The Board is also described as a move from universal multilateral institutions towards leader-centric mini-lateral mechanisms.
facts: UN peacebuilding missions often end once immediate crises subside
Prolonged deadlock over comprehensive UNSC reform has paralysed timely action
Under Article 22 of the UN Charter, the General Assembly can establish subsidiary bodies without Charter amendment
Board of Peace is presented as reform from within, not replacement of the UNSC
Board aims to institutionalise long-term political engagement and prevent relapse into conflict
Represents a move from universal multilateral institutions to mini-lateral, leader-centric mechanisms
Emphasises political authority, resource mobilisation and rapid decision-making over consensus-based diplomacy
Projected as a template for managing complex global conflicts
Signals evolving US thinking on conflict resolution and post-war governance

quizzes.passage: The Gaza war began in 2023. The United States has put forward a 20-point plan to end the war in Gaza. The plan carries the official title Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. It followed talks between President Donald Trump and Israel's Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The main aim is to bring the fighting to an end and to build a stable future for Gaza and its people. The plan describes Gaza's future in broad terms, and it sets out a sequence of steps for both sides to take. Essential goods are to reach the territory without delay, and damaged infrastructure is to be rebuilt. The economy is also to be revived, with jobs created and the region rebuilt as a place to live and work. The points cover security, aid, governance and reconstruction, and together they form one framework. Political arrangements form another part of the design. Day-to-day civil administration would pass to a temporary body of Palestinians working under a wider international board. The plan also points towards self-determination and statehood for Palestinians, and the United States is to lead talks on a peaceful political future between Israelis and Palestinians. Each part of the framework is set out in a numbered point in the plan.

quizzes.passage: A twenty-point plan has been proposed to end the war in Gaza. Its formal name is the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. Its proposer had held talks with the Israeli Prime Minister before putting it forward. The plan imagines a Gaza that is free of militant activity, so that it poses no threat to neighbouring states. Its early provisions concern a halt to military operations, the release of people held by each side, and the immediate entry of aid. The aid is meant to help rebuild essential infrastructure. The plan also proposes a special economic zone with favourable trade terms, which would be supported by outside investment and would generate employment. Gaza would be governed for a time by Palestinians working under an international board. The plan also points towards self-determination and statehood for Palestinians, with a peaceful political future to be sought through talks between Israelis and Palestinians. Each of these elements is set out as one of the plan's twenty points. The wider dispute has a long history, and Britain was granted a mandate over Palestine after the First World War. Gaza is described as a place where Israel's military would withdraw as stability grows. Gaza's residents are free to stay, leave or return.

quizzes.passage: A current affairs account treats reform of the United Nations system as urgent. Its argument begins with efforts to rebuild societies after conflict. Peacebuilding efforts often suffer from fragmentation and a loss of institutional continuity. In this setting, the Board of Peace is introduced as a US-led intergovernmental body with a transitional role in post-conflict Gaza. It works alongside the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza and the International Stabilization Force, supervising them and mobilising financial and technical assistance. The Board is also described as a new international body with its own charter, which covers membership rules, financial contributions and dispute redressal. Membership requires countries to consent to be bound by the charter. Membership can be rotational, and permanent membership is also available. Its stated objectives include transparency, coordination and accountability during Gaza's transition from conflict to reconstruction. Gaza's reconstruction is to be supported through a special economic zone with favourable trade terms. A Gaza Executive Board, described as a supporting operational body, coordinates activities on the ground. Day-to-day civil administration is handled by a committee of politically independent Palestinian technocrats. The plan also includes an interfaith dialogue platform. The wider dispute has a long history, and Britain was granted a mandate over Palestine after the First World War.

quizzes.passage: A current affairs account treats reform of the United Nations system as urgent. Peacebuilding efforts often suffer from fragmentation and a loss of institutional continuity. The Charter already allows a route for change, because the General Assembly may create subsidiary bodies without amending the Charter itself. This makes change faster than a full amendment process would be. The Board of Peace is presented as an example of this kind of innovation. It is described as a US-led intergovernmental body set up for Gaza's transition from conflict to reconstruction. It supervises a national committee for Gaza's administration and a stabilisation force, while mobilising international financial and technical assistance. The account stresses that the Board is meant to operate within existing arrangements rather than in opposition to them. The Board is intended to ensure transparency, coordination and accountability. Membership requires countries to consent to be bound by the charter. A Gaza Executive Board, described as a supporting operational body, coordinates activities on the ground. The account also notes that the Board signals changing thinking on how conflicts are resolved. Membership can be rotational, and permanent membership is also available. The wider dispute has a long history, and Britain was granted a mandate over Palestine after the First World War.
